_note: Tutorials for the play table (docs/tutorials-plan.md §3.6). Each step: at most 45 words, no digit outside a {placeholder} (rules/tutorialfacts.py), an anchor that is a data-tut attribute some template or script draws, and every control named by `controls` or `buttons` carrying that label near its data-tut. Change a step's words, anchor or controls and you must raise the tutorial's `v` and set that step's `since` to it, then refresh versions.lock (tools/tutorials_lock.py). tests/test_tutorials.py holds every rule.

steps.title: What do you do?
steps.words: Write what your character does, the way you would tell a GM, and press Say. The rules engine rolls and decides; the GM tells it. A turn takes a while on your own machine. A line starting /gm asks the engine out of character.

steps.title: Continue
steps.words: Continue means you keep doing what you were doing, and the world moves a beat. Use it when you have nothing new to say and want the scene to go on.

source.literal: I take no action. Carry the scene on from where it stopped

steps.title: The ways on
steps.words: These are the ways on from here. Press one to attach it to your turn, then Say to go; the time on it is real time passing. The suggestions below are offers, never orders: you can always write something else.

source.literal: A click ATTACHES the place, as a spell is attached, and Say sends it

buttons.label: Craft action
buttons.words: Forage, prospect, skin, gather or buy material, told as part of the story.

buttons.label: Spells
buttons.words: Casters only: choose a spell to cast with this turn.
Shows these tips again.

buttons.label: Map
buttons.words: Where everyone stands, and the places you have found.

buttons.label: Sheet
buttons.words: Your character: combat, skills, feats and the next level.

buttons.label: Equipment
buttons.words: Everything you carry, worn and held.

buttons.label: Spells
buttons.words: Casters only: what you know and have prepared.

buttons.label: Trade
buttons.words: Buying and selling, when you stand at a counter.

buttons.label: Journal
buttons.words: Quests, what people said, where you have been, and your notes.

buttons.label: Talk
buttons.words: What has been said to you, person by person.

buttons.label: Music
buttons.words: The soundtrack on or off; its level is in Settings.

buttons.label: Settings
buttons.words: Models, sound, tips and reporting a problem, without leaving the game.

buttons.label: Hide sheet
buttons.words: Folds the side panels away and gives the story the width.

buttons.label: Worlds & characters
buttons.words: Back to the shelf of worlds and characters.

steps.title: Who is here
steps.words: Everyone named here is in the scene with you, and so is anyone the story shows: you can speak to them, follow them or fight them by saying so. Press a name to see how they stand, unhurt or wounded, and anything on them.

steps.title: Getting material
steps.words: Every way of getting material where you stand, from every craft: forage, prospect, skin, gather or buy. Each is told in the story, with a real check and real time. One that cannot be done here is greyed, and pointing at it says why.

steps.title: Hours
steps.words: Set the hours before you press a way to gather. The ground underfoot, named at the top, decides what there is to find.

steps.title: Saying it instead
steps.words: You can also write a craft in the pen. Making a simple thing that way is a real roll and a real item, and the story then offers its bench for the full craft.

buttons.label: Work at the bench
buttons.words: Opens the herbalism bench over the table.

buttons.label: Open the full bench
buttons.words: Every craft's bench, on a page of its own.
Shows these tips again.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.words: Puts this away. Esc does the same.

steps.title: In hand and worn
steps.words: What you hold and what you wear, then your purse. Coins go by the names the nation you are in gives them, so the same coin is called something else across a border.

steps.title: The benches
steps.words: Each craft's bench opens over the table, and closing it keeps your place. Long work waits under In progress, below them, and finishes in its own time while you play.

buttons.label: Herbalism
buttons.words: The herb bench.

buttons.label: Smithing
buttons.words: The forge.

buttons.label: Enchanting
buttons.words: The enchanting circle.

buttons.label: Alchemy
buttons.words: The alchemy bench.

buttons.label: Leatherwork
buttons.words: The leather bench, with its vat and kettle.

buttons.label: Equipment
buttons.words: Everything you carry, on its own tab.

buttons.label: Crafting bench
buttons.words: Every craft's bench on a page of its own, away from the table.

buttons.label: Who is playing
buttons.words: Switch to another character; each one keeps their own game.

steps.title: Life and the body
steps.words: Your hit points, and any non-lethal damage against its own limit. Under them, thirst, hunger and rest count down their grace. Past it the body calls for rolls, and failing them costs you: eat, drink and sleep in good time.

source.literal: After the grace runs out, thirst asks every hour and hunger every day.

steps.title: Your numbers
steps.words: Abilities, defence and saves, as the rules count them now; a hurt ability says what it lost. The Sheet tab shows what each is made of.

steps.title: Experience
steps.words: How far you are from the next level, with your world classes under it. Once you have enough, the next full night's sleep takes the level.

source.literal: Any eight hours' sleep settles it

steps.title: Hide sheet
steps.words: Hide sheet folds both sides away and gives the story the width. Press it again to bring them back.

steps.title: Rolls
steps.words: Your own rolls from the latest turns, newest first: the die and everything added to it. What others roll is never shown here.

source.literal: Only the player's own rolls ever appear here.

steps.title: In the scene
steps.words: Who is in the scene and how they stand, and in a fight the turn order. Press a panel's name to fold it; it stays folded or open as you left it.

steps.title: The record
steps.words: An answer to a line starting /gm can carry The record beneath it: the engine's own account, word for word, rather than the GM's telling of it.

steps.title: Behind the screen
steps.words: The GM view, shown because its house rule is on: the schemes running in your world, what has fired and what is still to come. It shows the GM's secrets. Turn it off on the Rulesets bench.

steps.title: That’s wrong
steps.words: That’s wrong, under a beat, tells the game it got something wrong. Mark the wrong sentences and the latest beat is remade, or write it yourself; the engine’s own mistakes are logged too. Your turn is never taken back.

steps.title: Your roll
steps.words: This roll is yours: press Roll to throw it, or my own roll to type in a die you threw yourself. The lines show what adds to it. What others roll, and anything you could not know, is rolled out of sight.

source.literal: Only the player's own rolls ever appear here.

steps.title: Time passing
steps.words: When a turn takes an hour or more, a clock turns over the story to show the time going by, then goes; press it or Esc to put it away sooner. The day and the hour stay here, under the place's name.

steps.title: Whose words
steps.words: Everything said with the people here, or one person's words at a time. Earlier conversations keeps what was said with people who have gone.

steps.title: While you talk
steps.words: A conversation holds until you end it, and ending it is free. You answer by writing in the pen, as always.

buttons.label: Ignore
buttons.words: Stop answering one person who spoke to you.

buttons.label: Take your leave
buttons.words: End the conversation, at no cost.
Shows these tips again.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.words: Puts the tray away; Talk opens it again.

steps.title: Music
steps.words: Music turns the soundtrack on or off. How loud it plays is in Settings, with the other sounds.

steps.title: A death
steps.words: Death stays: the dead come back only if someone pays for a raising, and that offer comes first when there is one. Otherwise choose who plays next, or return to the main page; the game is kept as it stands.

source.literal: Death is a debt, not a wall

steps.title: Your sheet
steps.words: Every number on these cards is the engine's own, with what it is made of written under it. Combat comes first: your attacks, and each manoeuvre's bonus, rolled against the target's CMD.

steps.title: Skills
steps.words: Your skill totals. What each is made of shows the parts of every total; greyed skills cannot be tried untrained.

steps.title: Earn a living
steps.words: Work a day or Work a week earns pay at your trade. The pay is said before the roll, and the days really pass.

steps.title: Class
steps.words: Your class table, the paths you took and what the next level gives. Feats and traits, your deeds, and your background and notes follow below it.

buttons.words: Shows the tips for the tab you are on.

steps.title: A level to take
steps.words: When you have the experience, the next full night's sleep takes the level, or press Take level here. Choose the favoured class bonus beside it first. The hit points are rolled on the mat.

source.literal: Any eight hours' sleep settles it

steps.title: What it owes
steps.words: A new level can owe feats, skill ranks, ability points or class choices. They wait under To choose from your levels until picked, and each pick is checked against the rules as you make it.

steps.title: What you carry
steps.words: Everything you carry, A to Z, sorted onto shelves down the side. Each row has its own buttons, such as Wield, Wear, Take off or Use, and a row the rules cannot act on says why.

steps.title: Worn and wielded
steps.words: Every slot your body has. Press one to list only what fits it. Armour takes minutes to put on or take off, so in a fight only a shield changes.

steps.title: Food and drink
steps.words: Fill takes water where there is some; Eat and Drink answer hunger and thirst from what you carry. In a fight, a drink is your standard action and draws attacks of opportunity.

source.literal: a drink in a fight: a standard action that provokes

buttons.label: Go to Trade
buttons.words: New things are bought at a counter, on the Trade tab.
Shows these tips again.

steps.title: Slots
steps.words: Your slots by spell level, lit while unspent; cantrips spend none. A prepared caster may prepare whenever they like, but a slot spent today stays spent until a long rest.

source.literal: Prepare whenever you like. A slot

steps.title: Ready today
steps.words: The middle column holds what you have ready. Drag a spell into it, or press its Prepare or Learn button. Cast puts the spell on your next turn, beside the pen.

steps.title: What you can choose
steps.words: The last column lists what you can choose from, and spells a level owes your book wait across the top. A choice the rules refuse says why.

steps.title: Casting from the story
steps.words: The Spells button beside Say does the same from the table. Write what you cast at, and press Say.

steps.title: A counter
steps.words: Trade opens a counter only where someone keeps one; anywhere else this page says so. Where there is one, saying in the pen what you want to buy opens it by itself.

steps.title: The deal
steps.words: Put things from what you carry, or from their wares, into the deal, then press Trade. Prices move with how the keeper feels about you.

source.literal: make shop prices move with attitude too

steps.title: Haggle
steps.words: Haggle once a day at each counter: your Profession against the keeper's Sense Motive, for up to {haggle_max_percent} percent off what you buy, or onto what you sell.

steps.title: Trade goods
steps.words: Under the counter, goods by the pound: what this town makes, and where it sells dear. Carry them along the world's trade routes and sell where they are wanted.

buttons.label: Open equipment
buttons.words: Equipment, to wear or wield what you bought.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.words: Back to the table. Esc does the same.
Shows these tips again.

steps.title: Matters in play
steps.words: Matters in play are the things you have taken on: what is still to do, and what has happened so far. What people said keeps every conversation, a person at a time.

steps.title: What they have told you
steps.words: What companions confide about their own lives, once they think well enough of you. Where you have been lists the places you have walked.

steps.title: Notes and maps
steps.words: With ink and paper you can write notes here, or draw a map of where you have been. Without them, the buttons stay greyed.

steps.title: Further down
steps.words: History keeps what happened, day by day. Each craft you know adds its own book below it: the herbarium, the smith's ledger and the rest.

buttons.words: Shows these tips again.
